editorial:
You follow three American art students who head to a Slovakian hostel after a friend promises a relaxing getaway. At first, the place feels like a cheap party spot, but the smiles hide a dark business where rich clients pay to hurt travelers. The movie leans hard into shock and gore, so you should know what you are getting into before pressing play. It is not a mystery; it is a slow build into nasty surprises, with a grim mood that keeps you uneasy from the start.

The acting is solid enough to make the victims feel real, and the pacing keeps moving once the danger starts. The best part is how it shows both sides of the horror, which adds tension even when scenes get rough. The downside is that the gore can feel mean-spirited, and some twists are easy to guess. If you like extreme horror, you will have a wild time. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the sharpest picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Beth turns the tables on the client who bought her, kills him, and escapes the torture factory. She then takes revenge on the people running the auction and the recruiter who lured her group in. After settling the score, Beth gets away and survives the nightmare.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves extreme horror and dark revenge stories.
